messages.content: Produce a source-constrained implementation plan for the next patch to this Node ESM inference fabric. Return only the requested JSON. Current exact behavior: dispatchJobs(jobs, registry, options) validates jobs, then creates endpoint state Map entries {inFlight,next,cooldownUntil}, merged observations, one global worker pool, waiters/notify, and an inner jobRun. jobRun quote-plans one job, reserves endpoint concurrency and RPM slots, invokes a harness or OpenAI-compatible endpoint, verifies JSON/schema output, updates observations, falls through bounded candidates, and returns one record. dispatchJobs runs a finite queue with Promise.all(global workers), calls onRecord, and returns records+summary. dispatch-jsonl adds an output lock, append-on-completion checkpointing, history-derived observations, and resume by completed id. Problem: every dispatchJobs call recreates capacity/rate/cooldown/observations, and every workload requires an incumbent-authored batch process. Target: expose a long-lived line-oriented process that accepts one JSON job per stdin line, preserves shared scheduling state across submissions, emits one result JSON line as each job settles, supports concurrent submitted jobs up to the same global bound, bounds pending queue memory, rejects duplicate ids without duplicate provider spend, and can later be wrapped by ActivityStreams without changing scheduler semantics. Do not propose a filesystem watch directory or message broker. Choose a minimal refactor that preserves dispatchJobs as a compatibility wrapper. Name invariants and tests precisely; do not invent dependencies.

ids are removed from that Set only after the result line is flushed to stdout.","Back-pressure bound: the pending queue is capped at maxQueueDepth; submissions that would exceed this limit are synchronously rejected with a queue-full error result rather than silently buffered.","Result ordering is submission-independent: each result JSON line is written to stdout as soon as its job settles, not in submission order, preserving the line-oriented streaming contract.","dispatchJobs compatibility: the existing dispatchJobs(jobs, registry, options) signature continues to work by constructing a transient scheduler scoped to that call, so no existing caller is broken.","Stdin framing: each stdin line must be a complete JSON object with at least an 'id' field; a line that fails JSON.parse emits an error result line and does not terminate the process.","Global concurrency bound: the number of concurrently executing jobRun coroutines never exceeds the same globalConcurrency value that dispatchJobs enforces today; this is a property of the scheduler, not of a batch.","Graceful drain: receiving SIGTERM or {\"control\":\"shutdown\"} causes the process to stop accepting new jobs, drain all in-flight work, flush remaining result lines, then exit 0."],"implementationSteps":["Extract a createScheduler(registry, options) factory from dispatchJobs: move the endpoint-state Map, observations Map, global worker pool, waiter/notify mechanism, and jobRun closure into this factory; return { submit(job): Promise<ResultRecord>, drain(): Promise<void> }.","Add a pending-queue and in-flight-id Set inside createScheduler. submit() checks the id Set first (reject duplicate), checks queue length against maxQueueDepth (reject if full), pushes to the queue, wakes a free worker, and returns the settled promise.","Rewrite dispatchJobs as a thin wrapper: call createScheduler(registry, options), call scheduler.submit() for every job in the batch in parallel, await all returned promises, call scheduler.drain(), then assemble the existing records+summary return shape.","Create bin/inference-server.js: import createScheduler, read registry and options from argv/env, instantiate one scheduler, then open readline on stdin.","In the readline handler: JSON.parse each line (catching SyntaxError to emit error result line), enforce duplicate-id and queue-depth checks (emit rejection result lines immediately), otherwise call scheduler.submit(job).then(result => writeResultLine(result)).","writeResultLine(result) must acquire a per-process stdout write lock (a Promise chain, not a mutex library) before calling process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(result) + '\\n') to prevent interleaved partial lines under concurrent settlement.","Wire SIGTERM and {\"control\":\"shutdown\"} input to scheduler.drain().then(() => process.exit(0)); add a readline 'close' event handler that also calls drain then exits, so piped inputs terminate cleanly.","Update package.json bin field to point at bin/inference-server.js and add the maxQueueDepth option (default 1000) to the options schema validated at scheduler construction, not per-job."],"tests":["Scheduler state persistence: submit 3 jobs to one createScheduler instance sequentially, assert that endpoint inFlight counts never exceed the per-endpoint concurrency limit and that observations from job 1 are visible during job 3's candidate selection.","Duplicate-id rejection: submit job id='x', then before it settles submit id='x' again; assert the second submit resolves immediately with {id:'x', error:'duplicate'} and that only one provider call is made total.","Queue depth cap: set maxQueueDepth=2, saturate workers so the queue fills, then submit a third queued job; assert it resolves immediately with {error:'queue-full'} without a provider call.","dispatchJobs compatibility: call dispatchJobs with the same fixture used in existing tests; assert it returns {records, summary} with the same shape and that no scheduler state leaks between two successive dispatchJobs calls.","Concurrent settlement ordering: submit 5 jobs with staggered mock latencies; assert that result lines arrive on stdout in settlement order, not submission order.","Stdin framing - malformed line: write a non-JSON line followed by a valid job line to the server process stdin; assert an error result line is emitted for the malformed line, then the valid job is processed, and the process does not exit.","Graceful drain on SIGTERM: submit 2 long-running jobs, send SIGTERM; assert the process does not exit until both result lines are written, then exits with code 0.","stdout serialization: mock jobRun to settle 10 jobs simultaneously; assert stdout contains exactly 10 complete, individually parseable JSON lines with no interleaved bytes."],"principalRisk":"Long-lived cooldownUntil state can starve unrelated subsequent jobs indefinitely, whereas today each dispatchJobs call resets state. Fix: scope cooldown resets to per-endpoint TTLs from the provider retry-after header rather than relying on batch boundaries, and test that a job submitted after a cooldown window expires is re-admitted."}

invariants: Scheduler singleton: one Map<endpointId,{inFlight,next,cooldownUntil}>, one observations Map, one global worker pool array, and one waiters/notify closure are created once at process start and never recreated per dispatchJobs call.

Duplicate-id rejection: a submitted job whose id already exists in a pending-or-in-flight Set is synchronously rejected with an error result before any provider call is made; ids are removed from that Set only after the result line is flushed to stdout.
Back-pressure bound: the pending queue is capped at maxQueueDepth; submissions that would exceed this limit are synchronously rejected with a queue-full error result rather than silently buffered.
Result ordering is submission-independent: each result JSON line is written to stdout as soon as its job settles, not in submission order, preserving the line-oriented streaming contract.
dispatchJobs compatibility: the existing dispatchJobs(jobs, registry, options) signature continues to work by constructing a transient scheduler scoped to that call, so no existing caller is broken.
Stdin framing: each stdin line must be a complete JSON object with at least an 'id' field; a line that fails JSON.parse emits an error result line and does not terminate the process.

Global concurrency bound: the number of concurrently executing jobRun coroutines never exceeds the same globalConcurrency value that dispatchJobs enforces today; this is a property of the scheduler, not of a batch.
Graceful drain: receiving SIGTERM or {"control":"shutdown"} causes the process to stop accepting new jobs, drain all in-flight work, flush remaining result lines, then exit 0.
implementationSteps: Extract a createScheduler(registry, options) factory from dispatchJobs: move the endpoint-state Map, observations Map, global worker pool, waiter/notify mechanism, and jobRun closure into this factory; return { submit(job): Promise<ResultRecord>, drain(): Promise<void> }.

Add a pending-queue and in-flight-id Set inside createScheduler. submit() checks the id Set first (reject duplicate), checks queue length against maxQueueDepth (reject if full), pushes to the queue, wakes a free worker, and returns the settled promise.

Rewrite dispatchJobs as a thin wrapper: call createScheduler(registry, options), call scheduler.submit() for every job in the batch in parallel, await all returned promises, call scheduler.drain(), then assemble the existing records+summary return shape.
Create bin/inference-server.js: import createScheduler, read registry and options from argv/env, instantiate one scheduler, then open readline on stdin.

In the readline handler: JSON.parse each line (catching SyntaxError to emit error result line), enforce duplicate-id and queue-depth checks (emit rejection result lines immediately), otherwise call scheduler.submit(job).then(result => writeResultLine(result)).

writeResultLine(result) must acquire a per-process stdout write lock (a Promise chain, not a mutex library) before calling process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(result) + '\n') to prevent interleaved partial lines under concurrent settlement.

Wire SIGTERM and {"control":"shutdown"} input to scheduler.drain().then(() => process.exit(0)); add a readline 'close' event handler that also calls drain then exits, so piped inputs terminate cleanly.
Update package.json bin field to point at bin/inference-server.js and add the maxQueueDepth option (default 1000) to the options schema validated at scheduler construction, not per-job.
tests: Scheduler state persistence: submit 3 jobs to one createScheduler instance sequentially, assert that endpoint inFlight counts never exceed the per-endpoint concurrency limit and that observations from job 1 are visible during job 3's candidate selection.

Duplicate-id rejection: submit job id='x', then before it settles submit id='x' again; assert the second submit resolves immediately with {id:'x', error:'duplicate'} and that only one provider call is made total.
Queue depth cap: set maxQueueDepth=2, saturate workers so the queue fills, then submit a third queued job; assert it resolves immediately with {error:'queue-full'} without a provider call.

dispatchJobs compatibility: call dispatchJobs with the same fixture used in existing tests; assert it returns {records, summary} with the same shape and that no scheduler state leaks between two successive dispatchJobs calls.
Concurrent settlement ordering: submit 5 jobs with staggered mock latencies; assert that result lines arrive on stdout in settlement order, not submission order.

Stdin framing - malformed line: write a non-JSON line followed by a valid job line to the server process stdin; assert an error result line is emitted for the malformed line, then the valid job is processed, and the process does not exit.
Graceful drain on SIGTERM: submit 2 long-running jobs, send SIGTERM; assert the process does not exit until both result lines are written, then exits with code 0.
stdout serialization: mock jobRun to settle 10 jobs simultaneously; assert stdout contains exactly 10 complete, individually parseable JSON lines with no interleaved bytes.
structured_output.principalRisk: Long-lived cooldownUntil state can starve unrelated subsequent jobs indefinitely, whereas today each dispatchJobs call resets state. Fix: scope cooldown resets to per-endpoint TTLs from the provider retry-after header rather than relying on batch boundaries, and test that a job submitted after a cooldown window expires is re-admitted.
